_why: Engine-tile motion source manifest, in the shape site-films/broll/manifest.json already uses. The previous motion batch (1af78d9) recorded its recipe only in a commit message and committed no tooling, so the pipeline had to be rebuilt from scratch. Every clip here records the Higgsfield job id, the exact prompt, and the verification it passed. Job ids persist on Higgsfield's servers and re-download by id, so nothing needs regenerating (or re-charging) to reproduce this.
method: image-to-video from the tile's own poster (--start-image), so the artwork animated is the artwork already shipped

gates.rotation_span_deg: <=0.30 measured ON THE SOURCE RENDER at 1920x1080. The metric accumulates 120 consecutive-pair rigid fits and is resolution-dependent: the same clip reads 0.178deg at 1920x1080 and 1.771deg after a LOSSLESS downscale to 1280x720, while the shipped crf-30 file reads 1.478 -- lower than lossless, so it is tracking noise, not compression and not real motion. A pure resize cannot introduce rotation. Do not re-gate the shipped 720p file and conclude the batch regressed.
gates.handoff: frame 0 vs poster <8.0/255 mean abs, so the <video> replacing the poster does not pop
gates.aspect: clip aspect must equal poster aspect; these tiles are true 16:9 (1600x900), unlike the 1.791 tiles that needed refitting in 1af78d9
gates.footer_text: normalized cross-correlation of the burnt-in label ink, each frame against the clip OWN frame 0, >=0.90 on controls/tests/read-only. Absolute difference does not work: H.264 softening alone moves ink 15-20 levels, and a shadow crossing the strip reads as a redraw. part_no is advisory with a 0.55 floor because it sits at the longest lever arm from frame centre, so residual rotation displaces it most.
gates.loop_seam: every tile plays with loop=true, so the wrap from last frame to first is on screen every few seconds. install_motion.py eases the tail back to frame 0 (BLEND_FRACTION of the clip) so the wrap is continuous. Judge it in ABSOLUTE mean-abs terms, not as a multiple of the median frame step -- a nearly-static clip has a tiny median step, so an acceptable seam reads as '6x' while being visually nothing. All clips here land <=2.41; intercompany, which already ships and reads as a clean loop, is 2.11; the previous batch's upgrade/warranty/draw are 7-12.
gates.encode_order: close the loop in the SAME pass as scale+encode. A second pass over the finished 720p file costs a generation of H.264 and moved the handoff 3.8 -> 6.2 for no visible gain. Blending needs pixel access so the decode is unavoidable, but let ffmpeg scale: measured ffmpeg-only 3.69, python-decode+ffmpeg-scale 4.91, python-decode+cv2-resize 5.99.
gates.visual_review: REQUIRED, and not replaceable by any measurement. The numeric gates check the camera, the burnt-in figures, the handoff and the loop; none of them checks that the machine stays a machine. Of 30 clips passing all four, visual review found real defects in 16 -- paper draping like cloth, stacks draining and refilling, metal trays dissolving, a spring melting. spending and financing passed EVERY number on their final take (rotation 0.08/0.09deg, text intact) and were still obviously wrong on sight. Build a contact sheet per clip and look at it; unwire anything that fails.
gates.trim_tail: drift from the source frame grows with runtime: 1.5x higher at 90% of duration than at 30%, and most artifacts appear in the last third. install_motion.py drops the final sixth. That rescued inforeturn (report drooped only after frame 103). It does NOT fix early-onset defects -- checkage's paper melt starts at frame 17 -- those need a re-roll, and some tiles never converge.

bond.prompt: Treat the input as a locked-off studio photograph on a tripod. The camera is completely static: no orbit, no rotation, no pan, no tilt, no roll, no zoom, no push-in, no dolly, no parallax, no perspective change, no lens change. The machine body, the surface it rests on, the horizon line and the caption strip along the bottom edge are RIGID and must stay pixel-locked in exactly their original position, scale and angle for every frame. The bottom caption strip must remain perfectly horizontal and perfectly still; do not tilt, slide, skew, redraw or re-letter it. Animate ONLY small parts inside the open cutaway: the stack of pale workpapers at the left feeds forward one sheet at a time, inside the cutaway the collateral return loop with a release gate works steadily through one slow cycle, and the bound report at the right slides gently outward onto its tray. The round gauge needle sweeps slightly. Everything else in the frame is frozen. Subtle, restrained, precise mechanical motion, evenly paced for a seamless loop. Lighting, colour, matte cream background and metal finish unchanged. No people, no hands, no new objects, no text changes.

prompt_lesson: The attempt-1 checkage prompt said 'locked-off camera' but described the subject loosely; attempt 2 named the rigid parts explicitly (body, surface, horizon line, caption strip) and forbade tilt/skew/re-lettering of the strip by name. That is the difference between 1.75deg and 0.20deg. Use the attempt-2 wording as the template for the remaining 31, swapping only the mechanism sentence.
_why_not_animated: These tiles would not hold a locked-off camera or kept moving their own caption strip across repeated attempts. They keep their static poster rather than ship an animation that drifts or occludes a burnt-in figure; media.motion still equals media.poster for them, which is this repo's way of spelling 'no motion exists', so the generator emits no data-video.
